summary: A 60-ft steel lookout built by the CCC in 1933-34 in Franklin County, Tennessee; manned until the 1970s, now closed to climbers and used only for maintenance.

facts.design: 60-ft steel truss tower with 7x7-ft cab; register says International Derrick, nomination says Aermotor MC-39 type

staffing.status: unstaffed; no observation since the mid-1970s, occasional forestry maintenance climbs

access.note: Tennessee Division of Forestry site. The nomination (based on 2014 information) says forestry staff barred entry to the cab interior. No public visiting arrangement found.

visit.trail_note: No public visiting arrangement found in the sources; the nomination reports cab entry prohibited by forestry staff.

events.note: Register gives build year 1933 and says built by the CCC; nomination says construction began in 1933
Nomination says construction was completed in 1934 by the CCC
State forestry service contract with Adolph Hunziker dated July 13, 1934, allowing construction, use and maintenance of the lookout on the property
Radio tower #1 and radio equipment building erected about 1950 near the lookout
Approximate: nomination says the tower was constantly manned until the 1970s and no longer used for observance since the mid-1970s
Radio/cellular lattice tower constructed about 2010 on the site

The Sewanee Fire Lookout Tower was constructed beginning in 1933 with completion in 1934 by the Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) (Kirksey 2014).

evidence.supports: Aermotor MC-39 type by stylistic evidence, no manufacturer mark
evidence.quote: based on stylistic evidence the Sewanee Fire Lookout Tower appears to be a sixty-ft. Aermotor MC-39 type.

evidence.supports: MC-39 very similar to 1933 International Derrick
evidence.quote: This type is very similar to an International Derrick Tower model from 1933, which was designed by Aermotor and the United States Forest Service.

evidence.supports: tower part of TDF fire control program
evidence.quote: The tower was constructed as part of the Tennessee Division of Forestry's (TDF) statewide efforts to protect forested land in the state through its fire control program.

it is known that the State of Tennessee Forestry Service entered into a contract with Adolph Hunziker on July 13, 1934, which allowed the construction, use, and maintenance of a fire lookout tower on the property.

evidence.supports: very little history specific to this tower
evidence.quote: While very little historical information is available regarding the Sewanee fire lookout tower in particular

evidence.supports: used for detection and constantly manned until the 1970s
evidence.quote: Until the 1970s, the tower was used during high-fire season for fire detection, and was constantly manned.

evidence.supports: no longer used for observance since mid-1970s; occasional maintenance climbs
evidence.quote: Since the mid-1970s, however, when forestry employees became more dependent on fire-spotting planes and fire reports from 911 emergency calls, the tower is no longer used for observance, but is occasionally ascended by forestry staff for maintenance checks.

evidence.quote: Entry to the cab interior was prohibited by forestry staff.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register calls it an International Derrick tower. The nomination, judging by style and with no manufacturer mark seen, calls it an Aermotor MC-39 type that it says is very similar to the 1933 International Derrick design. The story reports both.
The register gives 1933 as the build year. The nomination says construction began in 1933 and was completed in 1934. The record's 1933 date is kept as the start of construction.
The register gives 2,039 ft (621 m). The nomination gives 2,044 ft. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Build date, design type and elevation conflict between the register and the NRHP nomination; both kept in the story. Current access and staffing rest on the nomination's 2014-era information, not a current site visit or Division of Forestry notice. The NRHP listing date was not confirmed from the sources read (NPGallery shows only a published date of 3/31/2015), so no nrhp_listed event was entered. No notable fires named in sources. No rental listing found. The record's 1933 'built' is kept; the 1934 completion is added as its own event.
